newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW-Rhone says $92 attractive for Rorer.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Rhone says $92 attractive for Rorer.

text.p: Rhone-Poulenc SA managing director Igor Landau said on Friday that the company still believed $92 per share to be "an attractive price" for Rhone-Poulenc Rorer shareholders in a planned buy-out.
Rorer shares have increased to above $93 from the $79 at which they were trading before Rhone-Poulenc announced on June 26 its intention to make a buy-out bid on minorities in the 68.3 percent unit.
It is currently awaiting the outcome of a study by a special committee of Rhone-Poulenc Rorer on the merits of Rhone-Poulenc's project.
"I re-affirm today that we feel the price of $92 is an attractive price to the shareholders," Landau said in a telephone interview.

"The next step is the following. We have announced our study, a special committee of Rhone-Poulenc Rorer has been created to study what they would do if we moved forward. They are at the moment studying and we most certainly will not move before having a discussion with them at the time that they will feel they are prepared and we will feel our studies are complete," Landau said.
"Then we will move forward, hopefully, if we decide so, with their agreement. But if they do not agree we will anyway make our own decision," he added.
